s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual onset of a painless, firm, and nonpulsatile mass in the thigh, fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin, with no signs of inflammation or neurovascular impairment
salient_findings: Painless swelling in the left medial thigh
Firm, nonpulsatile mass fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin
Well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass on CT scan with internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat
key_facts: 18-month-old girl
Swelling in the left medial thigh
Mass had enlarged gradually over six months
Painless mass
No history of trauma or infection
Firm, nonpulsatile mass measuring approximately 10 cm
Fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin
No signs of inflammation, neurovascular impairment, or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Laboratory tests were unremarkable
CT scan showed a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass in the left anteromedial compartment of the proximal thigh
MRI confirmed a fatty-appearing, well-circumscribed mass with internal septations and no encasement of neurovascular structures

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Fatty-appearing mass with internal septations on MRI, consistent with lipoma characteristics

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large, gradually enlarging mass with lobulated appearance on CT scan, raising concern for liposarcoma

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Firm, nonpulsatile mass with fatty appearance on MRI, consistent with fibrolipomatous hamartoma

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Painless, firm mass with fatty appearance on MRI, and absence of signs of inflammation or neurovascular impairment

shortlist.label: Angiolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Fatty-appearing mass with well-defined borders on CT and MRI, consistent with angiolipoma characteristics

raw.rationale: The mass is described as a firm, nonpulsatile, fatty-appearing lesion with internal septations, which is consistent with fibrolipomatous hamartoma, a benign tumor that typically presents as a slowly growing, painless mass in the thigh of young children.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: While lipomas can be large and painless, the presence of internal septations and the specific location in the thigh of a young child make fibrolipomatous hamartoma more likely.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Liposarcomas are rare in children and typically exhibit more aggressive features such as rapid growth, pain, and invasion of surrounding tissues, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
rejected.why: Pleomorphic lipomas are rare and typically occur in older adults, making them an unlikely diagnosis for an 18-month-old child.

rejected.label: Angiolipoma
rejected.why: Angiolipomas are typically small, painful lesions that are not consistent with the large, painless mass described in this case.
